deepdive.sec: Consumer Discretionary — Apparel / Specialty Retail (Women's Ethnic Wear)

bull_bear.body: - Post-IPO cash >₹30 cr; primary use = store rollout (Capex + working-capital inventory). No dividend/buyback discussion (newly listed). No leverage detail disclosed.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Guidance gap:** FY26 actual ~11% revenue growth vs 35% CAGR ambition — heavy reliance on un-built future stores + nascent online + un-signed MBO counters.
- **Soft/unverifiable guidance:** MD repeatedly deferred to slides; no hard FY27/28 targets; numbers self-reported, microcap SME.
- **Flat basket size** despite ASP rise — upsell execution risk.
- **Vendor concentration:** "few dedicated contract units" (mgmt downplays, cites supplier profiling & volume pricing power).
- **MBO dilution risk:** 28-32% margin to channel → bottom-line drag if mix shifts.
- **Execution/scale risk:** doubling COCO base + new formats (Divas/DIY) + global, all simultaneously, from a small base; aggressive 250-by-FY28 ambition.
- **Audio-quality / disclosure depth:** call had repeated audio issues; limited quantitative rigor.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: - Founder-led, visionary, promotional ("India's most accessible fashion luxury brand", "service-oriented brand"). Confident on store-expansion vision; evasive/qualitative on precise financial guidance (deflects to presentation slides). Honest acknowledgement of flat basket-value weakness. First-call enthusiasm.
bull_bear.title: Management tone

bull_bear.body:
- Brand was **acquired as a distressed asset during the pandemic** and re-platformed from pure offline EBO to omni-channel — turnaround story.
- Strategic intent to reposition as **service-oriented** (DIY studio, customization) rather than product-only — to defend ASP/loyalty.
- Nine99 outlets double as **demand-sensing scouts** for new full-line Kiaasa locations.
- Online is genuinely tiny (1-2%) despite "omni-channel" branding — physical EBO is the real engine.
- MBO explicitly accepted as margin-dilutive but pursued for footfall/awareness and EBO-conversion in shared malls.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious insights

business.body:
- **Core SKDS sets:** >50% of mix; primary revenue & margin engine; ASP ₹2,000-2,500.
- **Kiaasa Divas (kidswear 3-13):** new category, target 8-10% revenue.
- **DIY Studio:** ready-to-stitch boutique/service play (NOT tailoring); customer-engagement/gifting; target 4-5%→10-12%; needs 1,200-1,500 sq ft format.
- **Nine99 by Kiaasa:** sub-₹999 factory-outlet / liquidation tail of inventory cascade; 7-10 stores; small-town, single-staff, low rent/Capex, fast turnaround; recovers product cost; acts as scout for full Kiaasa EBO in nearby city.
business.title: Segment view

business.body:
- ✅ Beneficiary themes: last-mile logistics (Porter); contract garment manufacturers (Kiaasa-label suppliers); mall/high-street landlords in Tier-2/3; large-format/MBO channels (Reliance) gaining a SME ethnic brand.
- ⭐ (none confirmed — micro-cap, no clear listed downstream beneficiary call-out)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

latest_quarter.body:
- EBITDA margin 17.8% (+~400-500 bps YoY) driven by improved sourcing efficiency, bulk procurement vendor negotiation, operational cost control. Mgmt frames as new sustainable baseline with further upside over 5 yrs.
- ASP uplift via designer "signature stories" + keeping 10-15% higher-value SKUs; acknowledged **average bill value stayed flat despite ASP rise** → basket-size / upsell is a known weak spot (store-staff execution dependent).
- MBO margin caution: Reliance-type counters carry 28-32% trade margin → MBO will lift top line but **not** PAT/bottom-line (marketing/awareness play).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **H2/FY26 (this call):** First-ever earnings call (BSE SME listed Mar-2026). FY26 rev ₹134.63 cr (~+11% YoY), EBITDA ₹24 cr / 17.8% (+~400-500 bps), PAT ₹11.17 cr (+24%), SSSG 12.89% (vs 7.1%), 124 EBOs, >5.5 lakh customers, online 1-2%, post-IPO cash >₹30 cr. Guidance: 250 EBOs by FY28, ~300 by FY30; aspirational 35% rev / 45% EBITDA CAGR to FY30. New formats: Kiaasa Divas, DIY Studio, Nine99. MBO (Reliance) in discussion. No prior call for comparison.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **Store network:** 250 EBOs by **FY28** (vision); +66 stores over next ~2 yrs funded by IPO (COCO 110 → ~198); ~300 stores / +100 more by **FY30**. EBO count only — excludes MBO.
- **Revenue CAGR ~35% through FY30**; **EBITDA CAGR ~45% through FY30** (mgmt confirmed "yes, almost" to analyst; references presentation slide 20). Reconciliation of FY26's ~11% actual vs 35% ambition: future stores + online + MBO/LFS counters (600-1,000 LFS counters by FY30) to bridge the gap.
- **No explicit FY27/FY28 revenue or EBITDA rupee/margin targets given** — MD declined ("EBITDA target as such we don't have").
- **Segment mix targets:** Kiaasa Divas 8-10% of revenue; DIY Studio 4-5% initially → 10-12% in a couple years.
- **Store economics:** new store Capex ~₹24-25 lakh (varies by Tier/mall/high-street); avg size moving from ~700 sq ft → 1,200-1,500 sq ft for select larger-format stores (to house Divas + DIY).
- **Online:** ~1-2% now → 10-12% over a couple years.
- **Global (Dubai/London/Canada):** exploratory, 3-5 yr horizon, FY27-28 planning; COCO + FOFO mix; NRI-led inquiries.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — mgmt mostly soft/slide-deferred)

outlook.body:
- Tier-2/3 aspirational demand strong; market positioned as "value-conscious premium." Indian women's ethnic-wear TAM cited at ₹2.5 lakh cr by 2030, ~7% CAGR (claimed insulation from discretionary swings).
- Repeat-customer ratio 21-30% (avg ~30%); 70% still new customers → conversion-to-repeat is the SSSG lever.
- Mother-daughter duo upsell driving Kiaasa Divas rollout (tested in 25-26 stores last festive season, good response → pan-India).
- MBO pipeline: active Reliance discussion (~150 counters at 28-32% trade margin).
outlook.title: Demand / pipeline

outlook.body:
- Inventory-cascade model: premium malls → mid → Nine99 clearance, recycling capital, minimizing dead stock while protecting premium perception.
- Omni-channel: store-fulfilled online (geolocation routes to nearest store); Porter 2-hr delivery within 4-5 km, intercity 2-3 days; "real-time fresh stock online" (not discounted old-season) as differentiator.
- Optionality: MBO/LFS (Reliance, 600-1,000 counters by FY30) for top-line + brand awareness; global FOFO; larger-format lifestyle stores.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Newly-listed (Mar-2026, BSE SME) high-growth, asset-acquired affordable-luxury women's ethnic-wear brand running an omni-channel EBO model in Tier-2/3 India — using IPO proceeds to roughly double the COCO store base (124 → 250 EBOs by FY28), with margin expansion already delivered and an aspirational 35% revenue / 45% EBITDA CAGR ambition through FY30.
